items.note: RCT with 305 MBA students varying whether LLM support comes at problem formulation or only at ideation and evaluation; outcomes are the number of strategic alternatives (fluency) and their strategic focus. Abstract from Crossref (SSRN record); next stage should confirm a no-LLM arm exists.

Four online experiments (total N = 3,562, per-study N not in the abstract) where people collaborate with GenAI or work alone, then do a later task solo; abstract reports immediate performance gains that do not persist plus lower intrinsic motivation. Search notes say tasks include AUT and product-idea brainstorming rated for novelty and usefulness (possible after_ai outcome); verify in full text.

Per search notes, 2x2 between-subjects design with 176 university students (same- vs cross-discipline groups, with vs without GenAI) scoring individual and group creativity. Abstract not reachable (OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, Crossref, Europe PMC, Springer page all failed); a correction notice exists (10.1007/s10639-025-13878-x).

Classroom quasi-experiment: 27 architecture students in seven self-selected teams, four using a GenAI plus XR pipeline and three not; a seven-member panel rated team design presentations (no significant difference). Non-random and below 50 participants; outcome is presentation quality, not an explicit creativity score.

Per search notes, a mixed-design team ideation experiment varying AI content strategy (breadth- vs depth-first) and participation style (active vs passive), with divergent and convergent performance outcomes; one note reports N = 52. Abstract not reachable (OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, Crossref, Europe PMC, ScienceDirect); SSRN version 10.2139/ssrn.5246400. Compares AI configurations; no no-AI arm is mentioned.

Students in fine arts, literary writing, and fashion design were split equally into ChatGPT-4 intervention and standard-program control groups; creative potential measured with TTCT-Figural pre and post (unassisted test after AI use, an after_ai outcome). N and the assignment method are not in the abstract.

Controlled experiment with design students comparing a ControlNet sketch-scaffolding workflow with static moodboard ideation; blind experts rated line-art outcomes for design quality (d = 0.88). The sample size is elided in the retrieved abstract (Semantic Scholar); despite the title, the main outcome is rated output quality.

System paper (Scanvas) with a user study of 12 professional designers comparing the system with LLM ideation baselines on concept quality and synergy; AI-versus-AI comparison, no no-AI arm, well below 50 participants.

Two-stage design comparing Human-Only, LLM-Only, and LLM-Assisted writing on propositional and creative tasks, scoring originality and effectiveness; mostly a human versus LLM comparison, but the LLM-Assisted arm has people writing with AI. Assignment and N not in the abstract.

Title indicates an empirical study of AI's effect on creativity in L1 Chinese writing; abstract not reachable (OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, Crossref, Europe PMC, Elsevier blocked), so design is unknown and classified as experiment for full-text review.
